_readme: Regents West at 24th, 2401 San Gabriel St, as js/slopes-apartments.js draws it. Five storeys of student housing in a closed ring round one long courtyard: a burnt-orange retail and leasing storefront along W 24th St, four residential floors of recessed loggia balconies over it, punched windows on the quiet sides, a coral stair strip at the south-west, and a pale grey-green sloped cap round the whole roof with the white membrane and the rooftop terrace inside it. Metres in the footprint's oriented bounding box (js/westcampus.js obbOf): L=61.68, W=43.63, +u at bearing 184.7 deg, so u=0 is the NORTH end, +u runs SOUTH, v=0 is the EAST edge and +v runs WEST. Every number carries a _src naming a key in `sources`, or says derived or unknown. Read docs/apartments.md for the schema.
name: Regents West at 24th

sources.S1: data/snapshots/2026-08-27/buildings.detailed.geojson feature 70dcc366-e0b1-482d-aadf-937cbe06724e: name null, num_floors null, building_class 'residential', final_height 24.9, source_height 'overture'. The polygon has an outer ring and ONE inner ring - the courtyard. Wall trio wd #c0b39d / wg #cab395 / wn #333132, roof rd #756b5c. The 24.9 m is Overture's guess for a building OSM never tagged with a height, and this file overrides it - see levels._src.
sources.S2: OpenStreetMap relation 18074153 (multipolygon, building=residential, no name, no address, no height, no building:levels), queried from Overpass 2026-09-05. Its neighbours were queried in the same call: relation 18074152 is 'HillTop' on the far side of San Gabriel St and relation 18074154 is 2414 Pearl St, so 18074153 is the one building filling the block interior north of W 24th St between San Gabriel St (west) and Pearl St (east).
sources.S3: The three City of Austin address nodes that fall inside the outer ring - node 3842125041 '2401 San Gabriel Street', node 3842134980 '918 West 24th Street', node 3842134979 '912 West 24th Street' (Overpass, same call). 2401 San Gabriel St is Regents West at 24th; apartments.com, apartmentratings.com and the operator's own site all carry that address, and Google Street View (S6) shows the building's own projecting blade sign reading REGENTS WEST AT 24 over the 2401 door. This is what settles the identity - OSM itself carries no name.
sources.S4: yardimatrix.com property 31337 'Regents West at 24th, 2401 San Gabriel Street': 93 units, 101,175 sq ft, YEAR BUILT 2014. It does not state a storey count.
sources.S5: regentswest24.com (the operator) amenities page: 'Rooftop Terrace w/ Views of West Campus', 24-hour study lounge, clubhouse, fitness centre, Reserved Parking; umovefree.com's listing for the same property adds 'Community Parking Garage' and the floor-plan table (studio 430 sq ft up to 4/2 at 1,668 sq ft).
sources.S6: Google Street View on W 24th St looking north at the south elevation, imagery Mar 2025 (ref/sv-south.png in the session scratchpad, and the two crops r2/sv_s_left.png and r2/sv_s_right.png). This is the highest-fidelity source here and every storey count, floor height and ground-floor number below is read off it. It shows, bottom to top: the burnt-orange storefront band with NOW LEASING glazing, the ORANGE MARKET disc sign at the west end, the recessed 2401 entry and a blank orange wall east of it; four residential floors of recessed loggias with dark picket rails; a plain stucco band; and a sloped roof cap that overhangs the wall, dark from below.
sources.S7: Google Earth 3D, imagery 1/1/2021, captured 2026-09-05 with scripts/verify/chrome.mjs on hardware GL and page.screenshot(): a nadir at 180 m (ref/nadir-180.png, crop ref/c_nadir_bldg.png), obliques from all four quadrants at 333 m (ref/obl-sw.png, obl-se.png, obl-nw.png, obl-ne.png and the crops c_sw.png, c_se.png, c_nw.png), face-on captures at 278 m (ref/face-s.png, face-e.png and the crops c_faces_s.png, c_fe.png, c_swc_west.png, c_swc_south.png), and a close look down at the south end of the roof (ref/c_south_roof.png). The nadir is what the courtyard, the roof cap, the condenser clusters and the rooftop terrace were read off; the obliques are what the ring plan and the coral strip were read off.
sources.S8: data/roof_survey.json entry 70dcc366-...: roof area 2539 m2, mean roof colour (210, 211, 195), drop 0, and seven blobs - one 1231.8 m2 'plant' region 41.2 x 44.0 m covering most of the roof plane, and six small 'cond' units 0.9 to 1.9 m2 at (x, y) offsets from the centroid in metres. The six condenser positions are what roofItems below are placed from.
sources.S9: js/westcampus.js SOLID trios, the way The Standard's and The Castilian's files use them: the day/golden/night relationship for a deck, a roof and a mechanical unit.
sources.S10: A height fit against S7's nadir, run in the session scratchpad (fit.py). The outer ring is projected into the nadir at a trial roof height and its outline scored against a blurred gradient image, over h from 14 to 36 m and a plus or minus 9 m centring offset - a taller roof projects LARGER about the principal point, by 180/(180-h), so the fit is really measuring the roof outline's size. It peaks sharply: score 16.96 at h=19.5 m, and 7.33 / 13.63 / 16.83 / 12.65 / 7.47 at h = 16 / 18 / 20 / 22 / 24, falling to a flat 5.5 above 26. Overture's 24.9 m scores less than half the peak. The same script run on a nadir that had not finished loading returned a flat, meaningless profile, so this reading is only quoted for the frame that actually has the building in it.
sources.derived: a number computed from the above and marked so; 'unknown' stays unknown.

footprint._src: S1's OUTER ring verbatim. In (u, v) the six corners are (61.68, 0.00) (61.67, 43.60) (36.68, 43.63) (36.68, 39.05) (0.00, 39.08) (0.00, 0.06): a 61.68 x 39.08 m rectangle with a 25.0 x 4.55 m projection on the WEST side of its southern third. S1's INNER ring - the courtyard - is (39.86,27.78) (42.45,27.76) (42.39,19.32) (19.31,19.49) (19.34,25.50) (39.84,25.35), an L of 145 m2; the generator's `plan` takes no holes, so the courtyard is left as the gap between the five blocks below instead. Net area 2376 m2 against S8's measured roof area of 2539 m2 (S8 measures the roof, which oversails).

_frame_src: obbOf(ring) as the generator computes it: L=61.68, W=43.63, +u at bearing 184.66 deg. +u runs SOUTH (u=0 is the north end, u=61.68 is the W 24th St end); +v is 90 deg counter-clockwise from +u in (east, north), i.e. WEST, so v=0 is the EAST edge facing the Pearl St side and v=43.63 is the far WEST edge on San Gabriel St. The obb sits within 0.03 m of the ring at every corner - the outline is very nearly axis-parallel in its own frame - so every block below is entered as a rectangle. Confirm against the boot console line `[slopes-apartments] Regents West at 24th: obb L=61.7 W=43.6, +u at bearing 184.7`.

levels._src: FIVE storeys, not the eight that S1's 24.9 m implies. Read off S6, which shows the whole elevation against sky: one storey of orange storefront and then exactly four rows of loggia rail, with the roof cap above the fourth. The floor-to-floor 3.1 m is measured from the same photograph by the ratio of a floor pitch to the rail beside it, which are at the same distance and so need no scale: the level-3/level-4 pitch is 109 px against a 38 px rail, and a code rail is 1.07 m, giving 3.07 m; the level-2/3 pitch gives 3.2 m the same way. The ground floor is 4.9 m: 171 px from the pavement to the soffit of the level-2 balcony slab against 71 px for the 2.13 m entry door in the same plane. Two independent checks agree. (1) S4 states 101,175 sq ft = 9,400 m2 for 93 units; four residential floors over a 2,376 m2 plate is 9,504 m2 gross, which lands on it, while eight floors would be double the stated area. (2) The east elevation in S7's c_fe crop shows five window rows, one more than the south's four, because the level that is retail on W 24th is residential round the back - not because the building is taller.
levels._heights_src: eave 17.3 = 4.9 + 4 x 3.1, the top of the fourth residential floor and the head of the plain stucco band S6 shows above the top loggia. capTop 18.4 is the roof plane inside the sloped cap; the cap itself stands about 0.9 m above it (the parapet below), so the building's high point is 19.3 m. THAT NUMBER IS MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY: S10 fits the footprint's own outline to the roof edge in the nadir and peaks at 19.5 m, 0.2 m from the 19.3 m this file builds to, with Overture's 24.9 m scoring less than half as well. So three sources agree and one disagrees - S6 counts five storeys, S4's floor area allows four residential ones, S10 measures the roof edge at 19.5 m, and only S1's Overture guess says 24.9. Uncertainty about plus or minus 0.6 m, one third of a storey.

colours._src: day hex; golden and night follow js/westcampus.js's ramp() unless a full trio is given. Keys starting _ are notes. S6 is a mid-day Street View frame that reads about a quarter dark - its own concrete pavement medians #988c6c where a lit pavement is near #c8c4bc - so every hex sampled from it is named with its raw median and entered lifted by that much, and the lift is stated each time.

wall._src: S1's own wd for this building, the westcampus bake's measurement of this wall from imagery. It is entered unchanged so a mesh panel and the fill-extrusion band on the building next door age the same way. It agrees with S6 independently: the sunlit stucco cluster of the band under the eave is #958766 raw, #c2b085 lifted.

slab._src: the pale projecting slab edge under each loggia. S6, median of the level-4 slab edge (560,232)-(900,242) = #918969 raw, #bcb08a lifted; entered a step lighter still because that strip is the underside catching bounce, and it is the lightest thing on the elevation in the photograph.

trim._src: the cream window surround and reveal. Not separately sampled - it reads in S6 and S7 as the wall's own tone one step lighter, the way a painted stucco return does.

recess._src: the loggia interior in its own shade. S6, median of the level-4 balcony soffit (560,180)-(900,200) = #4e4325 raw; entered near the raw value because this surface really is in shade in every photograph, including the Google Earth mesh (S7), where the balcony bands are the darkest thing on the building.

balcGlass._src: the sliding door and side light at the back of a loggia. S6, median of (795,270)-(845,315) = #3a3828 raw, lifted; darker than the punched windows because it sits behind the balcony's own shadow.

glass._src: the punched windows, which read as a pale sage green in both sources - S6 (455,175)-(505,215) = #5b665d raw, and S7's mesh, where the window squares on the west and north faces are unmistakably mint against the tan wall. That green is the venetian blind behind the glass, not the glass, and it is what the building actually shows.

rail._src: the dark bronze picket rail on every loggia. S6, cluster of the rail zone (560,285)-(900,330): #3c3424 at 35 % and #2b2212 at 24 %, the pickets and the gaps between them; entered as the lifted picket value.

orange._src: the burnt-orange ground-floor band along W 24th St. S6, cluster of the blank wall east of the entry (760,620)-(930,750): the sunlit face is #9d5e2e at 56 %, the tree shadow on it #542b0f at 21 %. Entered as the sunlit value lifted one step. This is the building's one loud colour and it is the thing a passer-by names it by.

storeGlass._src: the dark shopfront glazing behind the NOW LEASING graphics. S6, (200,650)-(420,700) = #545347 raw, which is the graphic film rather than the glass; entered as the dark glass the unprinted panes read as.

coral._src: the vertical coral strip near the south end of the west elevation. S7, cluster of it in c_sw at (470,400)-(560,780): #86494c at 38 % with the shaded side at #5d4642. Entered as the lit value lifted; the Google Earth mesh reads it consistently in the SW, SE and NE obliques, so it is a real painted plane and not a texture artefact.

cap._src: the sloped roof cap SEEN FROM ABOVE, which is how the app's oblique sees it. S7, cluster of the band along the top of the south and east walls in c_se (300,330)-(800,420): #adaca8 at 31 % and #d4d8d7 at 27 %. From the pavement the same cap reads dark - S6's (300,80)-(700,105) is #3a3221 - because from there you see its shaded underside; that value is `capShade` below and the two are the same material.

capShade._src: the same cap's fascia from below, the band S6 shows between the top windows and the sky. S6 raw #3a3221, lifted; entered as the wall's top band so the eave line reads from a walking camera as well as from above.

membrane._src: the white roof inside the cap. S7 nadir, cluster in c_sw (700,150)-(950,300) = #cfd4d4 at 37 %; S8's mean roof colour for the whole plane is (210, 211, 195) = #d2d3c3, measured independently by the roof bake. The two agree, so the entered value is between them.

colours._deckTone_src: the rooftop terrace paving at the south end. S7, cluster of the deck in c_south_roof (300,500)-(900,570): #a7a69f at 45 % and #adaca4 at 41 % - weathered concrete pavers, not membrane. Golden and night entered the way S9 enters a deck.

railWhite._src: the pale guard rail round the roof terrace, the row of light pickets across the south edge of the roof in S7's c_south_roof. Not separately sampled - entered as the deck's own tone lifted.

colours._furniture_src: the dark loungers and tables on the terrace deck (S7, c_south_roof, where they are the only dark blobs on a pale plane). A SOLID trio in S9's manner.
colours._condenser_src: S8 gives the six roof units' colours between (173,176,159) and (254,254,239) - mid grey to white galvanised. The trio is S9's mech tone, as The Standard's and The Castilian's files use it.

penthouse._src: the stair penthouse at the north end of the roof (S7 nadir, c_nadir_bldg top centre, a small pale box with a warm cap). Entered as the wall tone one step lighter; not separately sampled.

sign._src: the white lettering on the projecting blade sign over the 2401 entry (S6). The blade's own backing is dark - see signBack.

signBack._src: the dark backing panel the blade's letters sit on (S6); entered as the rail tone, which is what it reads as at this distance.

balcony._src: THE BALCONIES HERE ARE RECESSED, not projecting: S6 shows the rail standing at the wall plane with the room set back behind it, and the only thing that comes forward is the slab edge, about a third of a metre. So `proj` is 0.32 m, which is the slab's own oversail, and the depth of the loggia is carried by the `recess` tone and the 0.35 m reveal of the `loggia` skin's opening instead. railH 1.05 m is the code rail S6's pickets measure (and the number the floor height was derived from, so it is not free); slabT 0.30 m is the slab edge in the same photograph, 10 px against the 38 px rail.

skins._src: one rule per face treatment; every count comes from a module, never a hard-coded number.

loggia._src: The loggia elevations - the south face on W 24th St and the east faces of the two end wings (S6, and S7's c_fe where the same dark bands run). One loggia per unit; the 4.0 m bay is the unit width read off S6 by counting the privacy divider positions across the south face, ten of them in 39.1 m. The opening is 3.1 x 2.25 m on a 0.5 m upstand - the glazed slider plus its side light, which S6 shows filling almost the whole bay between dividers - set 0.35 m back, so the loggia reads as a hole rather than a window. The 0.34 m slab line at every floor is the projecting edge S6 draws as the strongest horizontal on the building.

punched._src: The quiet elevations: north, west, the middle of the east side and all four courtyard walls (S7's c_swc_west, c_fe's centre bay, c_nw). A near-square window a shade taller than wide, one per 2.1 m. The module is half the 4.0 m unit bay: the photographs show the windows loosely PAIRED within a unit rather than evenly spaced, and at this app's oblique - about 0.3 m per pixel, so a window is four pixels - an even 2.1 m run and a pair at 4.2 m are the same picture. Said plainly so a later pass with a real elevation drawing can put the pairing back. Size read off c_swc_west against the 3.1 m floor pitch: the squares are a little under half a floor tall.

store._src: The W 24th St ground floor: leasing office, study lounge and fitness centre behind a continuous shopfront in a burnt-orange stucco band, with the Orange Market at the west end (S5 lists the amenities, S6 photographs the frontage and its own NOW LEASING graphics list them). Mullion 1.7 m is read off S6 by counting nine panes across the glazed run. The band's solid tone and the fascia are both the orange, because in S6 the orange is the wall the shopfront is punched into, not a stripe above it.

orangeFlat._src: the blank orange wall east of the 2401 entry, and the orange returning round the south-east corner (S6). No glazing at all in that stretch.

coralFace._src: the coral strip near the south end of the west elevation, which every Google Earth oblique (S7) shows running the full height with a column of narrow dark slots in it - a stair. The slot size is read off c_sw against the 3.1 m floor pitch and is uncertain by about 0.3 m; the strip is 4.6 m wide there, so it carries two slots a floor.

crown._src: the band between the head of the top windows and the eave: plain stucco in S6, and in shade under the cap's overhang in every ground-level view. It stands in for the underside of the sloped cap, which the generator has no primitive for; the cap's own lit face is carried by the parapet above, in `cap`.

blocks._src: The north wing of the ring, u 0 to 19.3 across the full 39.08 m width. Its u1 face at u=19.3 is the courtyard's north wall; the parts of that face buried behind the east and west wings are left drawn because they are back-to-back with those wings' own faces, which the generator's header says is safe, and nulling them would take the courtyard wall with them.

v0._src: the east elevation of the north wing, which S7's c_fe shows wearing the same loggia bands as the south face. The balcony run is the face's whole length less half a metre at each end.

blocks._parapet_src: the 0.9 m upstand stands in for the sloped cap that rings the roof: S7's nadir shows a pale grey-green band about a metre wide inside every roof edge, mitred at the corners, with the white membrane inside it. Not a parapet the building has - a cap the generator can draw. The courtyard edge (u1) gets none because the east and west wings stand on it at the same height.

roofItems._src: S7 nadir (c_nadir_bldg, top centre): a small pale box with a warm cap standing on the north roof - the stair and lift head. Size read off the gridded nadir to about plus or minus 1.5 m.
S8's condenser blobs at centroid offsets (-13.8, -5.8), (-16.0, 6.8) and (-13.8, 26.1) fall on the north wing's roof; S7's nadir shows them in loose rows along the east side of it.

blocks._src: The east wing, u 19.3 to 42.4 and 19.4 m deep from the Pearl St side - a double-loaded range. Its v1 face is the courtyard's east wall. Its u0 and u1 faces are nulled because the north and south wings' own faces already close those ends. S7's c_fe reads the east elevation as loggia bands at the two ends with a plain punched bay in the middle; this middle wing is that punched bay, so it keeps the block's default skin.

The west wing north of the projection, u 19.3 to 36.68 and 13.7 m deep from the San Gabriel St side - a single-loaded range, which is why it is shallower than the east one. Its v0 face is the courtyard's west wall.

roofItems._src: S7 nadir: the west roof strip carries a run of units along its whole length, which S8's small 'cond' blobs corroborate.

blocks._src: The short piece of the west wing that the projection stands against, u 36.68 to 42.4. It exists as its own block only so that the projection can null a whole face instead of half of one - the generator can null a face but cannot null part of one, and two same-facing coplanar walls z-fight.

The south wing on W 24th St, u 42.4 to 61.68 across the 39.08 m width of the main rectangle. This is the elevation the whole neighbourhood sees and the only one with a source better than photogrammetry. Its u0 face is the courtyard's south wall; its v1 face is nulled because the projection stands against it.

signs._src: the projecting blade over the 2401 door in S6, which reads REGENTS WEST AT 24 down a dark backing panel. Only the first word is set here: at 0.09 m a dot the seven letters are 5.0 m of sign, which is the blade's own height in the photograph against the 3.1 m floor pitch, and the whole legend would be three times that. It is centred on the face because the entry is within a metre of centre in S6 and the two balcony runs are placed to leave it clear.

u1._src: S6, the whole stack: 4.9 m of orange shopfront, then four floors of loggia, then the shaded band under the cap. The two balcony runs stop 1.2 m short of the entry bay on each side, which is where S6's blade sign and the recessed door break the rail line.

v0._src: the east elevation of the south wing: S6 shows the orange returning round the south-east corner as a blank wall, and S7's c_fe shows loggia bands above it, the mirror of the north wing's east face.

roofItems._src: S7 nadir: a band of units across the roof just north of the terrace; S8's blob at centroid offset (10.1, -28.1) is in this run.

blocks._src: The 25.0 x 4.55 m projection on the west side of the southern third - the one thing in the outline that is not a plain rectangle (S1's outer ring). It is drawn full height, the same 18.4 m as the rest: S6 shows the wall at the west end of the south face running from the pavement to the cap with no step, and the outline is one building in one polygon with one height in S2. The alternative reading - a low wing, which S7's nadir hints at with a tan lower roof near this corner - is not taken, because that tan patch sits outside the red outline when the footprint is overlaid and is more likely the small building next door. Say so plainly; a Street View frame from San Gabriel St would settle it in one look.

overrides._src: the coral strip: a 4.6 m wide full-height plane near the south end of the west elevation, with a column of narrow slots in it. S7 puts it two thirds of the way along the west side towards W 24th St in the SW, SE and NE obliques alike; the u range here is read off c_sw against the 61.68 m length and is uncertain by about 2 m. The region contains only this stretch of the projection's own v1 wall, so it cannot leak on to another face.

deck._src: The rooftop terrace S5 advertises and S7's c_south_roof photographs from above: a paved deck across the south end of the roof, a pale guard rail along its south edge, and clusters of dark loungers and tables on it. Everything below is read off that one frame against the 39.08 m width, to about plus or minus 1.5 m.

items._src: the paving: concrete pavers, not membrane - S7 measures it #a7a69f against the roof's #cfd4d4
the pale guard rail along the deck's east edge in c_south_roof
the same rail returning along the west edge
the rail across the deck's north edge, the line of light pickets that separates the terrace from the plant deck in c_south_roof
a lounger; S7 shows six or seven of them in two loose rows along the deck
the table and chair cluster at the south end of the deck

_open: The bump's height is the one real risk: full height on the strength of S6 and the OSM polygon, against a hint in S7's nadir that the roof is lower at that corner. A Street View frame from San Gabriel St looking east settles it.

The courtyard is entered as the gap between the five blocks at 23.1 x 6.0 m, from S1's inner ring. S7's nadir reads the dark slot wider than that, nearer 9 m, but the extra is the sloping courtyard wall catching light rather than the opening, and the traced ring is the better number.

The punched windows are entered on an even 2.1 m module where the photographs show them loosely paired within a 4.2 m unit bay; at this app's cameras the two are the same picture, and a real elevation drawing would let the pairing be put back.
Nobody has photographed the four courtyard walls or the north elevation from the ground; both wear the plainest skin the building has.
The blade sign is set as REGENTS only. The full legend on the building is REGENTS WEST AT 24.
